page: UpCloud PREMIUM-2xCPU-16GB is a virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is provisioned with 2 shared vCPUs based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9575F processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 16.0 GB of system memory, which yields an 8.0 GB per core ratio. The CPU topology features 1 thread per core and includes modern instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16), SHA-NI, and AES cryptography acceleration. The instance does not include a GPU accelerator and bundles 150 GB of local SSD storage alongside one public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional single-thread processing capabilities contrasted with limited multi-core throughput due to the low physical core count. The instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng single-core performance (3756.97), single-threaded gzip compression (38.22 GB/sec), bzip3 decompression (17.95 GB/sec), and Geekbench single-core testing (2248.0). Memory bandwidth remains in the average tier, with 68.14 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 50.81 GB/sec for large-block writes. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks such as the PassMark CPU score (5994.86), Geekbench multi-core (4044.0), and Clang compilation (4552.0) score in the lower percentiles.

Given its 1:8 core-to-memory ratio, the instance offers strong memory density relative to its processing footprint, though the shared CPU allocation creates potential contention tradeoffs. The hardware profile is efficient for memory-dependent tasks that rely on single-threaded execution rather than high-throughput parallel computation. It is appropriate for workloads such as medium-sized memory caches, single-threaded backend services, text processing pipelines, lightweight databases, and static web serving, but it is not intended for heavy multi-core compilation, physics simulations, or medium-to-large LLM inference.
description: UpCloud PREMIUM-2xCPU-16GB is a KVM-based virtual server configured with 2 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor at 2.0 GHz and 16.0 GB of RAM. The x86_64 architecture incorporates AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware flags, accompanied by 150 GB of local SSD storage and no GPU accelerator. With an 8.0 GB per core memory footprint, the instance exhibits top-tier single-core performance, delivering strong scores in Geekbench single-core, single-threaded gzip compression, and text processing benchmarks. However, the 2-vCPU ceiling limits multi-threaded throughput, resulting in lower scores on multi-core compilation, ray tracing, and larger LLM inference tasks. This configuration is well suited for memory-intensive applications requiring strong single-thread performance, including in-memory caching, text parsing, lightweight databases, and general web services.
